welcome.description: Startup splash. If Plymouth is active during boot, Cinemate waits for it to hand off before showing this so the screen transition stays clean.

image.description: Path to a bitmap logo, e.g. /home/pi/welcome_image.bmp. Overrides message when set.

enabled.description: true broadcasts this hotspot on boot. false still serves the web UI on wlan0/eth0 if that interface already has an IP when Cinemate starts.

web_api.description: HTTP/UDP control API over the Wi-Fi hotspot (docs/web-api.md). A missing or partial block behaves as the defaults shown here.

allow_destructive.description: false blocks reboot/shutdown/erase/format over the API. The hotspot password ships as 11111111, so this defaults to false.

auto_preroll.description: Warm media automatically before the first take. See docs/storage-preroll.md.

recovery.description: Standalone recovery console (its own root systemd service) for diagnosing and repairing a Cinemate that will not start. Reachable over the hotspot at http://10.42.0.1:8080. See docs/recovery-console.md. A missing block behaves exactly as the defaults shown here.

token.description: Required on every mutating request once non-empty. Read-only pages (status, log, why) stay reachable without it.

allow_config_txt.description: false hides the config.txt editor. A bad config.txt can make the Pi unbootable, and nothing running on the Pi can recover that -- so this defaults to off.

config_confirm_timeout_s.description: Seconds to confirm a config.txt change before it auto-reverts and the Pi reboots.

sensors.description: Per-sensor hardware: geometry, HDMI output, name spoofing, phase lock, CineMate Log, and the sensor metadata database.

record_policy.description: Dual-sensor record policy. follow_preview: recording follows the HDMI preview -- a full-screen or pip-main sensor records alone, side-by-side records both. always_both: force both sensors every take regardless of preview. A camera token on `rec` (rec cam0/cam1/both) overrides either policy for one take. No effect with a single sensor.

database_file.description: Sensor metadata database -- every mode each sensor supports (see image_capture for the filter that picks which ones show in the UI).

settings.description: Frame-rate conform target, flicker-free input, and sync tolerances.

light_hz.description: Mains frequencies to derive flicker-free shutter angles from.

arrays.description: One block per cycle-able camera parameter. steps is the selectable table; free steps continuously instead, in units of free_increment. See module/parameters.py:REGISTRY for the canonical name list (iso, shutter_a, fps, wb, hdr_threshold_low, hdr_threshold_high, hdr_blend, hdr_gain_adder). shutter_a additionally has sync_increment, its own granularity used only while shutter-angle sync mode is on (`set shutter a sync`), independent of free_increment.

free_increment.description: Step size used when free is true, e.g. 0.1 for fine sub-degree shutter-angle control.

image_capture.description: Resolution / bit-depth / HDR filters offered by `set resolution`. A filter, not the mode list itself -- see sensors.database_file.

hdr.description: ClearHDR (imx585) whitelist plus startup values for the live knobs. sdr/imx585_clear_hdr both true exposes the plain and the HDR modes; set imx585_clear_hdr false to hide the HDR modes. threshold_low/high (0-4095), blend (0-8), gain_adder (0-5) seed the ClearHDR knobs when a ClearHDR mode is selected -- adjust live afterwards with `set hdr threshold low/high`, `set hdr blend`, `set hdr gain adder`, or a pot/quad-rotary channel.

24bit.description: Settings for the 24-bit USB dsnoop path (RØDE NTG, mic_24bit alias)

16bit.description: Settings for the 16-bit plain-arecord fallback path (generic USB PnP mics)

hdmi_display.description: HDMI canvas, GUI overlays, and preview zoom/source/pip/anamorphic.

mirror_to_both_ports.description: Single-sensor only: mirror the one sensor's preview (with GUI) onto both HDMI connectors. The dual-sensor compositor already owns both-feed layouts, so this has no effect with two sensors attached.

default_hdmi_source.description: Dual-sensor HDMI preview source at startup. Switch live with `set preview`. No effect with a single sensor.

hardware_controls.description: Direct-GPIO physical inputs, channel-first: buttons, switches, rotary encoders, combined actions.

input_peripherals.description: Grove Base HAT analog pots and the Adafruit quad I2C rotary encoder board.

hardware_outputs.description: Direct-GPIO outputs Cinemate drives: the REC tally/relay pin(s) and the REC sync tone.

output_peripherals.description: The optional I2C OLED status screen.

phase_lock.description: Enable the cinepi-raw frame-rate phase lock for this sensor (holds the recorded cadence on the nominal fps for stable A/V sync). Safe to leave enabled on multi-camera --sync genlock rigs: cinepi-raw runs the lock only on the master (--sync off/server) and the --sync client self-suppresses so libcamera's rpi.sync owns that sensor's VBLANK.

tuning_file_override.description: Override the libcamera tuning file for this sensor

log_encode.description: CineMate Log recording target for this sensor. false = off (default, opt-in only). true = on, using the live source bit depth's default target (16-bit -> 12, 12-bit -> 10). 10 or 12 = on, forcing that target explicitly -- applied only when the sensor's live source bit depth actually supports it (e.g. 10 to force 16-bit ClearHDR down to 16to10 instead of its 12 default); never silently substituted to a different target. Only sensors with a sensors.json log_encode block (currently imx585, imx283) support this -- the setting is ignored on other sensors.
